lines: +# Client-stack gate
+`check.sh <candidate-venv>` exits 0 iff the candidate (harbor+litellm) is
+interchangeable with the pinned reference `/opt/venvs/client` (harbor 0.24.0,
+litellm 1.99.4) for everything we launch. Otherwise exit 1 with a diff report.
+## What it runs
+`gate.py` (in the reference venv) runs `harness.py` in both venvs, 4 groups
+in parallel: the TB2.1 eval config for each checkpoint in
+`/app/launch/checkpoints` (kwargs built via the exact `--ak` strings of
+`run_tb21_eval.sh` and the candidate's own `parse_kwargs` + agent factory),
+both RL rollout modes from `/app/launch/rollout/terminus_agent.py` with
+recipe.env values (GRPO: Miles request kwargs; token mode
+`HARBOR_COLLECT_ROLLOUT_DETAILS=1`: `collect_rollout_details`,
+fixed session id, extra-body top_p/top_k), the 12 recorded episodes in
+/app/episodes replayed through the agent loop (responses synthesized from
+the recorded analysis/plan/commands/reasoning; observations replayed into a
+fake tmux session), synthetic messy traffic, and targeted probes.
+The harness drives the real Terminus-2 + LiteLLM stack of each venv against
+a scripted OpenAI-compatible fake server (with SSE support, and token-id /
+logprob fields gated on the request like SGLang) and a scripted terminal,
+and records every request.
+## Scenarios cover
+Calm multi-turn runs (JSON and XML parsers, interleaved thinking on and
+off); reasoning variants (empty/absent/whitespace/inline `<think>`);
+parse errors, warnings, auto-fixes and the double task-complete handshake;
+truncated output (XML salvage behaviour included); context-overflow
+summarization via exact SGLang error wordings, fallback rungs, proactive
+summarization in a long rollout; transient, persistent and connection-drop
+errors, 401 auth errors (retry counts); max-turns termination from
+recipe.env; terminal timeouts and session death; >10 KB and unicode/ANSI
+terminal output; empty/aborted responses, missing-usage variants; plus
+`collect_rollout_details` response shapes (prompt/response token ids and
+logprobs as SGLang returns them).
+Probes compare `parse_kwargs` output, job `RetryConfig` defaults, LiteLLM
+`token_counter` (which sets summarization timing), context/output limit and
+hosted-vllm validation, rollout `TrialConfig` construction via the real
+rollout module, direct LLM error-type mapping and retry counts, the JSON/
+XML parsers, output length limiting, reward-file parsing through
+`Verifier.verify()` (including NaN/inf/empty/missing/precedence), and the
+tmux session layer's exec commands and output diffing via a recording fake
+environment. Agent option defaults (summarization threshold, pane size, …)
+are compared per config.
+## What counts as "the same"
+Every captured request is canonicalized the way SGLang's chat endpoint
+computes it for the corresponding served model (templates/tokenizers from
+`/app/launch` and `/models`, with `enable_thinking`/`preserve_thinking`
+pinned exactly as `serve_policy.sh` pins them):
+- conditioning: the exact prompt token ids after its validated message
+  normalization (roles, content-parts handling, tool-call serialization,
+  reasoning rules) rendered through the served Jinja template and
+  tokenized with the served tokenizer. Equalities that follow from the
+  template (reasoning dropped, inlined or extracted by the template) count
+  as equal, and so do string vs text-part message encodings.
+- sampling: effective parameter set after SGLang's defaults: temperature,
+  top-p, top-k, min-p, penalties, max/min new tokens, stop strings/regex/
+  ids, n, seeds, logit bias, grammar constraints, skip/no-stop-trim and
+  related flags. `max_tokens` vs `max_completion_tokens` is the same
+  parameter; omitting a field that defaults to the sent value (e.g.
+  `top_p: 1.0`) is the same; dropping a non-default value (e.g. a missing
+  `top_k: 20`) is not. Unknown or return-only fields that SGLang ignores
+  (`user`, stream flags, logprob-return flags, unknown extras) are
+  ignored here too; requests SGLang would reject (e.g. `top_k: 0`) count
+  as "server-invalid", distinct from valid ones.
+- counts: the full ordered sequence of requests per scenario.
+## Trial outcome
+Per scenario the gate compares the agent's outcome: the exact sequence of
+keystroke batches (with durations) sent to the terminal (which determines
+what the downstream verifier will grade), whether the run finished cleanly
+or with an exception of the same type name (what the trainer records),
+episode and summarization counts, collected rollout details (token-mode
+training data), and trajectory contents (messages, reasoning, tool calls,
+observations, continuation/summarization split files). Pure bookkeeping
+noise is not compared: timestamps, session UUIDs, cost/token accounting,
+and agent version strings.
+## Live stage
+When `ENGINE_URLS`, `ENGINE_LOG_DIR` and `GATE_REPORT` are set, every
+request the replay produces (first all reference requests in scenario
+order, then all candidate requests) is re-sent to the corresponding SGLang
+server with an injected deterministic `rid`; generation is aborted once
+SGLang has received and tokenized it, so the stage stays prefill-only.
+Prompt token ids and sampling then come from the `request.received`
+records SGLang writes to `ENGINE_LOG_DIR` (response `sglext.input_ids` is
+only a fallback for records with no ids) instead of the gate's own
+renderer. `GATE_REPORT` is written as `{"prompt_ids_sha256": [...]}` with
+one hash per re-sent request, in send order, of the id list SGLang
+recorded (hash of the empty list when it recorded none).
+What the gate does not check: environment/sandbox behaviour (Modal, the RL
+broker) and wall-clock effects (agent/version timeouts duration, retry
+backoff timings, throughput). Work directories with the full raw runs are
+kept under the `client-gate-*` temp dir named in the output line.
